ANALYSIS: These are distinct sexually transmitted infections with different etiologies, clinical courses, and management. Lymphogranuloma venereum (Chlamydia trachomatis L1–L3) classically causes a transient or unnoticed genital lesion followed by progressive unilateral inguinal/femoral lymphadenopathy (buboes), possible "groove sign," and proctocolitis in receptive partners.
